Triage: `pm:queue` + `domain:engine-core` + `target:v17`.

- **Landing**: the fix is a registry API change in `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` — verified on `origin/main` @ `271cee1` that `unregisterObjectsByPackage` (registry.ts:1339) is the only removal verb and the `objectContributors` map (registry.ts:916) has no per-(type, name) unregister; the heal `restoreArtifactRegistryView` (metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:7876) operates on the generic metadata map only. A name-addressed unregister honouring the ADR-0029 owner/extender rules lands in objectql, with a small call-site change in the protocol heal ⇒ engine-core lane.
- **target:v17**: board class ① — live on the ordinary Studio path today: delete a runtime-created object and the process keeps serving and accepting writes for it (`getObject` is the data-CRUD dispatch surface) while its `sys_metadata` row is gone. Silent data-wrong.
- **Dedup**: #6725 is the write side of the same map-vs-contributors split (dormant; both bodies state the fixes are disjoint). #6780 (queued, `domain:metadata`) is the org-blind eviction defect in the same heal — disjoint fix, same seam: the dispatch prompt for either card should flag same-seam coordination (serial or explicit file-face disjointness vs the other card's PR).
- **Stale-premise**: all anchors re-verified at `origin/main` @ `271cee1` (issue measured @ `4bb6f01af`).

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

**Next in line, not yet dispatched (engine-core seat #6019, session `session_01MwoubC3jL271FYt9rGXwxb`).** The lane is at **batch:1** by maintainer instruction (17:3xZ) and the single slot currently holds #6810 (the other new `target:v17` card). This one takes the slot next.

Ordering rationale, so it does not read as neglect: #6810 is an unambiguous injection-site fix with a ruled direction; **this card needs an API decision first** — as the body says, `SchemaRegistry` has no per-`(type, name)` object unregister at all, only `unregisterObjectsByPackage(packageId, force)`, so closing it means introducing a name-addressed `unregisterObject` that honours ADR-0029's single-owner/extender rules. That is a registry contract addition, and the PM will state the shape as a ruling in the dispatch (with the alternative — routing the heal through a package-scoped path — priced against it) rather than leaving a dev to invent it mid-task.

Severity is not in question and is arguably above #6810's: a deleted object stays **dispatchable, syncable and writable** for the life of the process because `getObject` — the surface data CRUD dispatches on — is the half the heal misses. Both delete-shaped callers are affected identically.

Two things this card should carry when it flies, recorded now so they are not rediscovered: PR #6807 (#6621) wired `revertCommit`'s soft-remove limb to the same heal, so its behaviour moves with the fix; and the `getItem('object', …)` special-case back to `getObject` is why listing looks clean while dispatch does not — the pin must assert **both** exits.

File surface: `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (the new name-addressed unregister + `objectContributors` removal), `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` — **only** `restoreArtifactRegistryView`'s object limb (the call site), tests in both, `.changeset/`. ⛔ Nothing else in `restoreArtifactRegistryView` (see the same-seam note), ⛔ no spec change, ⛔ `unregisterObjectsByPackage` keeps its current signature and semantics.
Serial constraints cleared: `registry.ts`'s landings today (#6786, #6788, #6794) are all MERGED; #6812 (#6810, also `registry.ts`) is in the merge queue **ahead of this card** — the dispatch requires merging `origin/main` before opening the PR, and again if #6812 lands mid-flight. Same-seam coordination flagged by triage: **#6780** (`domain:metadata`, org-blind eviction in the *same* heal) — disjoint fix, and this claim's file face is narrowed to the object limb precisely so the two PRs cannot collide; the metadata seat's card may proceed in parallel.

**PM ruling — the API shape (第三档: ruled, with a named falsifiable premise; veto window open).**

Take the **name-addressed unregister** (`unregisterObject(name, …)` on `SchemaRegistry`, honouring ADR-0029's single-owner/extender rules: refuse — loudly, not silently — while an extender still depends on the owner, mirroring `unregisterObjectsByPackage(force)`'s existing judgement rather than inventing a second one). Rejected alternative, priced: routing the heal through the package-scoped verb would mean synthesising a package identity for a runtime-created object and would tear down every sibling object registered under it — a wider blast radius than the delete the operator asked for, and it would leave the seam's real gap (no per-name removal exists) unclosed for #6725 and every future caller.

Rationale on the three axes: **business need** — the demand is measured and shipped-path (delete on the Studio path leaves the object dispatchable/writable); **long-term** — `registerObject` has had no inverse since it existed, which is why the heal could only clean half the split; adding the missing verb closes this card and gives #6725's write-side seam its natural landing later; **AI-safety** — a removal verb that refuses loudly on a live extender is learnable, whereas today's silence (delete succeeds, object still serves) is the failure class this repo keeps closing.

**Premise the dev must verify first (falsifiable):** that a name-addressed removal can honour the ADR-0029 rules with the information `SchemaRegistry` already holds (owner + extenders per object), without a new bookkeeping structure. If it cannot, STOP and report the fork with evidence — ⛔ do not invent a parallel ownership index, and ⛔ do not fall back to the package-scoped route silently.

Container judgment: size M-L (registry API addition + protocol call site + two delete-shaped callers to keep at parity) ⇒ `mode:cloud`.

## os-dev final report (#6808)

Draft PR: #6818 (branch `claude/issue-6808-registry-unregister-object`, merged with `origin/main` at `578bdef`).

**Premise verdict: VERIFIED.** A name-addressed removal honours ADR-0029 with what `SchemaRegistry` already holds — `objectContributors: Map<fqn, ObjectContributor[]>` carries `{ packageId, ownership, priority, definition }` per contribution, so the owner and the extenders are one `find`/`filter` away on the list the removal is about to touch. No parallel ownership index, no fallback to the package-scoped verb.

**What shipped.** `SchemaRegistry.unregisterObject(name, { force })` — the name-addressed removal that did not exist — plus the heal's object limb calling it from tier 3 only, for a name that is not artifact-backed. The ADR-0029 refusal mirrors `unregisterObjectsByPackage`'s judgement with the address changed from package to name; `unregisterObjectsByPackage` itself is untouched.

**One thing worth the reviewer's eye.** Self-review of the first version of the limb found a hole in it: on a control-plane kernel the two-tier delete authorization does not run, and the **no-row leg** of `deleteMetaItem` reaches the heal without touching the repository's `assertAllowed` either — so the walk could arrive for a name a code package still ships and unregister it, taking that object off the whole data plane until restart. The limb now carries the same artifact refusal `removeOverlayEntry` applies one line up, asked through the protocol's own `isArtifactBacked`. Pinned on both sides, with the tenant-kernel `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` refusal pinned as its pair.

**Left open deliberately:** #6725 (noted in the PR body — the new verb is its natural landing later), and one adjacent *restoration* gap described in the PR's scope notes (nothing re-registers a packaged contributor definition once an overlay save has replaced it; undecidable at this seam with the information the walk has).

**ACCEPT (engine-core seat #6019, session `session_01MwoubC3jL271FYt9rGXwxb`).** PR #6818; CI verified directly on the latest head `635c0e9e` — 24/24 concluded, zero non-green, ESLint + TypeScript Type Check both `success` (three intermediate pushes were main merges; the verdict is taken on the final head, not an earlier run).

The ruled shape landed with its premise **verified rather than assumed**: `objectContributors` already carries `{ packageId, ownership, priority, definition }` per contribution, so owner and extenders are one `find`/`filter` away on the very list the removal touches — no parallel ownership index, no silent fallback to the package-scoped verb, and `unregisterObjectsByPackage` untouched. All four acceptance criteria are pinned as specified: both exits stop serving (plus `getAllObjects`), CRUD refusal asserted by **identity** (`OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` / 404 / object name, with the data-row count unchanged), the extender guard refuses **naming every extender** and leaves the object intact, and #6807's parity comparison stays green while `objectServed` is now asserted **false outright on both sides** — the pin asserts the fixed view rather than freezing the old one, which is exactly what was asked.

**The self-caught hole is the part worth naming.** The first version of the limb would have let the walk arrive for a name a code package still ships — on a control-plane kernel the two-tier delete authorization does not run, and `deleteMetaItem`'s no-row leg reaches the heal without touching `assertAllowed` either — taking that object off the **whole data plane until restart**. Finding that in self-review, fixing it by asking the protocol's own `isArtifactBacked` (the same refusal `removeOverlayEntry` applies one line up), and pinning both sides plus the tenant-kernel `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` pair is the difference between closing this card and opening a worse one.

Scope held exactly: #6780's org-blind-eviction lines untouched (the same-seam coordination worked), spec unchanged, #6725 left open with the new verb recorded as its natural landing. Two reverse-verification passes, 10/10 and 2/2 signature-exact. The restoration gap it declines to fix — nothing re-registers a packaged contributor definition after an overlay save replaced it — is correctly described as undecidable at this seam with the information the walk has; the PM will file it as a finding for triage.

Now: ready + auto-merge; issue closes on merge. `target:v17` board item cleared.
